chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Al-Mukhtar, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Every banner that is raised before the rising of Al-Qaim, its owner is a tyrant who is worshipped besides Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of rulers before the rise of Al-Qaim?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines pre-Qaim political authority as 'taghut,' emphasizing that their rule constitutes a form of idolatry where worldly power is worshipped alongside or instead of Allah. This concept is central to Shia eschatology, distinguishing the legitimate, divinely-guided rule of the Mahdi from the usurped, often tyrannical, authority of previous eras. It underscores the theological weight of political allegiance, framing obedience to pre-Qaim rulers as a test of faith.
